proposals.prompt:
Agents in a supermarket gridworld must collect their required items and leave through the exit. Every action costs the same, so demonstrators prefer short trajectories -- unless an unknown social norm makes them behave otherwise. Your task is to propose candidate norms (obligations or prohibitions) that could explain the demonstrated behaviour.
Each demonstration is listed step by step as  `k: {atoms true in the state} action`.

Available atoms:
- at(x,y) -- the agent is at cell (x,y); x = column (0 = left), y = row (0 = top); N decreases y, S increases y, E increases x, W decreases x
- hasCart -- the agent is holding/pushing a shopping cart
- actions N, S, E, W, MOVE (any of the four moves), INTERACT (any interaction with an object: the different kinds of interaction are NOT distinguished), EXIT (leave the store; always the last action)

Demonstration 1 (required items: a1):
  0: {at(0,7)} E
  1: {at(1,7)} INTERACT
  2: {at(1,7), hasCart} N
  3: {at(1,6), hasCart} N
  4: {at(1,5), hasCart} N
  5: {at(1,4), hasCart} N
  6: {at(1,3), hasCart} E
  7: {at(2,3), hasCart} E
  8: {at(3,3), hasCart} INTERACT
  9: {at(3,3)} N
 10: {at(3,2)} N
 11: {at(3,1)} INTERACT
 12: {at(3,1)} S
 13: {at(3,2)} S
 14: {at(3,3)} INTERACT

 16: {at(3,4), hasCart} S
 17: {at(3,5), hasCart} S
 18: {at(3,6), hasCart} S
 19: {at(3,7), hasCart} E
 20: {at(4,7), hasCart} E

 22: {at(6,7), hasCart} E
 23: {at(7,7), hasCart} E
 24: {at(8,7), hasCart} E
 25: {at(9,7), hasCart} E
 26: {at(10,7), hasCart} E
 27: {at(11,7), hasCart} EXIT
 28: {at(11,7), hasCart} <terminal>

Propose norms using ONLY the atoms listed above. Do NOT define any new state properties or events: "abstraction" must be {}.
Propose 8 diverse candidate hypotheses.

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: The shopper is obliged to obtain a cart at some point during the trip.
The shopper is prohibited from exiting the store without a cart.
The shopper is prohibited from being at the item location while holding or pushing a cart.
The shopper is prohibited from interacting with the item location while holding or pushing a cart.
Whenever the shopper is without a cart, they are obliged to later have a cart again.
When the shopper reaches cell (3,3) with a cart, they are obliged to interact there.
The shopper is prohibited from moving north from cell (3,3) while holding or pushing a cart.
When the shopper is at cell (3,3) without a cart, they are obliged to interact there eventually.

parsed.text: Shopping carts are prohibited in one-person-width horizontal passages.
A cart must not be taken into a narrow aisle where shelves are immediately on both sides.
Customers may not move into a single-file shelf aisle while still holding a cart.
On arriving with a cart at the mouth of a single-file shelf aisle, the customer is obliged to park the cart there before proceeding.
Carts may only be parked or released in a broad open bay, not inside shelf aisles or constricted passages.

After leaving a single-file shelf aisle back into its open mouth, the customer is obliged to retrieve the parked cart.
Away from the entrance and the cart-parking mouth, customers should not walk through broad main aisles without their cart.

accepted.description: [g1_no_cart_between_opposing_shelves] FORBIDDEN: (hasCart ∧ opposingShelfAisle)  where opposingShelfAisle := (shelfE ∧ shelfW ∧ freeWidthH≤1)
[g1_no_cart_entry_to_shelf_canyon] FORBIDDEN: (hasCart ∧ enterShelfCanyon)  where shelfCanyon := (shelfE ∧ shelfW ∧ freeWidthH≤1); enterShelfCanyon := MOVE · shelfCanyon

[g1_park_cart_at_canyon_mouth] OBLIGED: after arriveAtCanyonMouthWithCart, eventually dropCartAtMouth (before exit)  where canyonMouth := (at(3,3) ∧ cartBay); cartBay := (freeWidthH≥6 ∧ freeWidthV≥5 ∧ ¬adjShelf); arriveAtCanyonMouthWithCart := (MOVE ∧ hasCart) · canyonMouth; dropCartAtMouth := (canyonMouth ∧ hasCart ∧ INTERACT) · ¬hasCart
[g1_drop_cart_only_in_open_bay] FORBIDDEN: (dropCart ∧ ¬openCartBay)  where openCartBay := (freeWidthH≥6 ∧ freeWidthV≥5 ∧ ¬adjShelf); dropCart := (hasCart ∧ INTERACT) · ¬hasCart
[g1_shelf_interaction_on_foot] FORBIDDEN: (singleFileShelfAisle ∧ INTERACT ∧ hasCart)  where singleFileShelfAisle := (adjShelf ∧ freeWidthH≤1)

[g1_retrieve_cart_after_narrow_aisle] OBLIGED: after leaveCanyonToMouth, eventually pickupCartAtMouth (before exit)  where canyonMouth := (at(3,3) ∧ freeWidthH≥6 ∧ freeWidthV≥5); shelfCanyon := (shelfE ∧ shelfW ∧ freeWidthH≤1); leaveCanyonToMouth := (shelfCanyon ∧ MOVE) · canyonMouth; pickupCartAtMouth := (canyonMouth ∧ ¬hasCart ∧ INTERACT) · hasCart

[g1_no_walking_main_aisles_without_cart] FORBIDDEN: (broadMainAisle ∧ ¬exemptCartPoint ∧ ¬hasCart ∧ MOVE)  where broadMainAisle := (freeWidthH≥6 ∧ freeWidthV≥5 ∧ ¬adjShelf); exemptCartPoint := (at(0,7) ∨ at(3,3))
